recentItems.title: Baghdad's annual agriculture Expo draws local, regional and international companies
recentItems.description:
(27 Aug 2026) 
IRAQ AGRICULTURE EXPO

SOURCE: ASSOCIATED PRESS

RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

LENGTH: 3:20

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Baghdad – 25 August 2026
1. Top shot of agricultural exhibition at Baghdad International Fairgrounds
2. Tractors displayed at the exhibition
3. Kurdish farmer showing his plants
4. Various of visitors at the exhibition 
5. Various of people visiting different sections
6. Various of agricultural products on display 
7. SOUNDBITE (English) Baker Khalid, technical commercial engineer at Debbane Agri in Lebanon:
“The importance of our participation in the 17th week of agriculture in Baghdad, comes from our belief that supporting the farmers is part of our duty jointly with the governmental organizations. That’s why we are here, to bring our experience more than 75 years in agriculture to the Iraqi farmers, to solve major problems caused by the climate change, and to be next to the farmers.”

8. Various of participating companies in the exhibition
9. Wheat samples and fertilizers on display in company section 
10. Wide of participating company stand, Terra Peat, selling organic products
11. Various of tractors on display in the exhibition
12. Various of sprinklers and irrigation systems 
13. Close of small Iraqi and Turkish flags 
14. Agricultural equipment on display in the exhibition 
15. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Omar Bader, visitor from Baghdad:
“Regarding the displayed products inside the exhibition; I saw the high-quality products from various Arab and foreign countries. We saw (products) from Yemen, the (United Arab) Emirates, Turkey, China, and Iran. This shows that Iraq has opened its doors for agricultural trade with different countries.”

16. Various of the Saudi section in exhibition
17. Various of dates displayed for visitors
18. Various of vegetables and fruits displayed
19. Various of the Iranian section in the exhibition
20. People walking outside the exhibition venue
STORYLINE:
Local and international companies flocked to Iraq's agricultural week, presenting products and sharing insights at a busy exhibition. 

The event in its 17th edition saw participation from neighboring countries such as Turkey, Saudi Arabia and global powerhouse China. 

The space was filled with large tractors, sprinklers, fertilizers and all kinds of agriculture equipment. 

This year's theme was sustainable farming, and different stands promoted organic vegetables, fresh fruit and dates. 

Baker Khalid, a technical commercial engineer in Lebanon, said he participated in the exhibition in an effort to support the Iraqi agriculture sector as it faces various challenges, including climate change. 

"That’s why we are here, to bring our experience more than 75 years in agriculture to the Iraqi farmers," he added.

The exhibition ended on Wednesday. 

AP video by Ali Jabar

recentItems.title: John Cena discusses his new film '12 Rounds'
recentItems.description:
(21 Jul 2009) 

STORYLINE:
SHOTLIST
London, 20th April 2009
6 mins approx
1. Sitdown interview with John Cena including the soundbites:
John Cena - on why he agreed to do the role:
"I liked the story and I thought it was very reality based.Nowadays a lot of the action movies certainly try to raise the bar on stunts they can do, or I don't know, I would say bend the laws of realism. We tried to put together a good story that everyone could follow, and that they could look at and say 'You know what, that's pretty possible'. I mean some of the scenarios are getting close but you can watch the movie and it's- I think that's why it's so suspenseful and I think that's why people are on the edge of their seat because they can see themselves almost making this stuff happen."
John Cena - on doing his own stunts
"All the action was me. There were some instances that I couldn't participate in things, but really, most of everything - I think there was one jump to the helicopter that I couldn't do, and a small bit of driving that they wouldn't let me do just because they were afraid that the car was going to blow up, but I pretty much got involved in everything."
John Cena - on similarities training for film and wrestling.
"The training was the same, but I mean instead of, you know, getting in there and body slamming somebody, I'm hanging off the side of a streetcar or climbing out of police cruiser to go inside a street car, I mean it was different action, you know, it is action, it's physically pushing yourself but it's not inside a wrestling ring."
John Cena - on having to work at height despite his phobia:
"It just got done.  It was one of those things I was kind of asked politely to do it and told that I could turn it down but I really, we had a really good crew and I really made friends with a lot of people there so I said 'I'll suck it up and do it' and it got done, but I certainly, it was a couple of long days of work."
John Cena - on his fan base in wake of his various activities (wrestling, film and music) and looking to future film projects.
"I also look at the fan base now and see that it is primarily kids as well, so in searching for the next project I think something geared towards more the kids, especially being in the UK, seeing our audiences just really, really young kids, and I think that speaks volumes for our WWE programming. It's certainly I feel comfortable saying it's entertainment that anyone can watch. And I think in searching for the next film project it will be something to cater to that audience."

recentItems.title: Alfonso Cuaron, Carlos Cuaron, Gael Garcia Bernal and Diego Luna discuss their new film 'Rudo & Curs
recentItems.description:
(21 Jul 2009) 

STORYLINE:
SHOTLIST
London, 22nd June 2009
TAPE ONE
5 mins approx
1. Sitdown interview with Alfonso Cuaron and Carlos Cuaron including the soundbites:
SOUNDBITE ( English ) Carlos Cuaron, Director:
"It made it easier, at least for me, you know, the fact that we are all close friends, that we know each other so well, that we are like this family of friends.  It saves you a lot of time, but also its just the trust, you know, and the camaraderie that happens and the whole atmosphere during the shooting was amazing."
SOUNDBITE ( English ) Alfonso Cuaron, Producer
"And everybody there for the same reason and you know, with the same goals, it was very easy. At the end, everybody was there because they really wanted to be there."
TAPE TWO
7 mins approx
1. Sitdown interview with Gael Garcia Bernal and Diego Luna including the soundbites:
SOUNDBITE ( English ) Gael Garcia Bernal:
"The storyline of the characters was very clear, but the context, the colouring of the characters we sort of developed it together with Carlos (Cuaron) by going, first scouting to where we were going to shoot it and deciding on a certain series of rules for the characters, especially too with the accent. We saw there in the banana plantations, a lot of people we talked to them and then we just mixed many things. I mean, the accent was completely invented. That was really fun to do. That was incredibly fun and we had a lot to play with. A lot, a lot to play with. Many things came into place and of course when we look at the movie, there's many jokes that construct the character."
SOUNDBITE ( English ) Diego Luna:
"When the storyline is clear, then you can really spend your time just using your imagination and finding these characters. And once you find it, I mean - it took a long time to say goodbye to these characters. Even today, I miss a little bit of Rudo."

recentItems.title: A surge in Canadian defense spending boosts local military contractors
recentItems.description:
(27 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMAMRY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
North York, Canada - 20 July 2026
1. Close of woman working at sewing machine
2. Wuxly founder and CEO, James Yurichuk, holding helmet cover, UPSOUND (English):
 “So these are Canadian-made helmet covers. It’s a work in progress right now, see all these threads need trimming down, but there’s a lot of engineering - here’s a complete garment - a lot of engineering goes into here, you see the quality.” 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Mississauga, Canada - 20 July 2026
3.  SOUNDBITE (English) James Yurichuk, Wuxly founder and CEO: 
++PARTLY OVERLAID BY SHOTS 4 AND 5++
“We're certainly excited to hear about Prime Minister Carney's D.I.S. Strategy and the defense boom. We're seeing it quite evident at all the events we're at. Every defense show sold out. Lots of new companies and industries coming into the industry, getting involved, the banks, finance. We also implore them to look at the clothing systems. This is so important. There's a lot of innovation that can create advantage in the North, and with the Arctic region being so important, we've got to clothe our soldiers properly.”
4. Close of jacket pocket 
5. Various of Wuxly employee trying on military jacket

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Kleinburg, Canada - 13 July 2026
6. Various of Volatus drone

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Vaughan, Canada - 13 July 2026
7. SOUNDBITE (English) Glen Lynch, Volatus CEO: 
++PARTLY OVERLAID BY SHOTS 8 AND 9++
“The objective is to develop the technologies that the Canadian Armed Forces needs, which are also including kinetic products, because those are required and they have to be built in Canada. So the FPV, what they call kamikaze type drones, we have some products for that. We have some interceptor drones. But largely, if you said, where do you focus as a company? We focus on things that are truly dual use, which means we can apply them on the commercial side, we can also deploy them on the defense side. So we're really, we try to meet all of the requirements of the Canadian Armed Forces.”  

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Kleinburg, Canada - 13 July 2026
8. Volatus workers preparing heavy lift drone for test
9. Close of propeller
STORYLINE:
A worker feeds white camouflage fabric through a sewing machine. 

Velcro strips are carefully attached to the material, specially designed to blend in in Arctic settings. 

This garment factory in a suburban Toronto industrial park is producing helmet covers for the Canadian military. 

The team are assembling uniforms for Wuxly, a luxury parka maker that is among a flurry of Canadian companies branching into defense contracting. 

“It’s a work in progress right now, says James Yurichuck, Wuxly’s founder, as he turns over one of the helmet covers.”  

“See all these threads need trimming down, but there’s a lot of engineering.” 

As Canadian military spending surges, others are developing remote sensors for the country's vast Arctic region, making drones to resupply soldiers, and building autonomous robots.

The boom in the defense sector reflects Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's vow to strengthen the country's economic self-sufficiency amid fraying relations with Washington, including a fresh escalation this week with new rounds of tariffs.

Canadian startups and established companies, alongside firms in Europe, are set to benefit from tens of billions of dollars in extra defense funding, driven partly by pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump to contribute more to NATO. 


A defense industrial strategy released earlier this year by Carney earmarks an additional $60 billion in funding over the next five years.

recentItems.title: Burnham says UK will be there for Nepal 'in its hour of need' after catastrophic floods
recentItems.description:
(27 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

UK POOL 
South Wales, UK - 27 August 2026
++STARTS AND ENDS ON SOUNDBITE++
1. SOUNDBITE (English) Andy Burnham, UK Prime Minister: 
"These are such distressing scenes coming out of Nepal and we feel for the people there and everything that they're going through at this moment in time, such devastation of communities and already sadly it seems such huge loss of life. In the past Nepal has been there for Britain in our hour of need and we will be there for Nepal in its hour of need right now. So the immediate offer that the Foreign secretary has relayed to the Nepalese government is an offer of first responders, search and rescue support, Britain excels in this and we're there and ready to be deployed, obviously it's a matter for the Nepalese government, but that is available. Financial support has been put on the table as well of course. British nationals missing as well and we need to support that search and rescue effort. We're also redeploying Foreign and Commonwealth office staff from the wider region into Kathmandu so that there is 24/7 consulate support for British nationals in the country but of course their families back here at home who are obviously going through some really difficult moments right now.  So a comprehensive package of support has been put forward, but we'll continue to work closely with our colleagues in the Nepalese government over the coming hours and days and obviously we all hope and pray for everybody affected by these devastating events."
++ENDS ON SOUNDBITE++
STORYLINE:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Thursday that Britain has offered search-and-rescue teams and financial support to Nepal after catastrophic floods that have left hundreds of people missing. 

Rescue teams searched for hundreds of missing people along the Nepal-Tibet border after the collapse of a glacier sent a deadly wall of water and mud several stories high tearing through communities on Wednesday. 

At least 273 people were killed, more than 1,300 are missing, including foreigners and pilgrims, and hundreds have been displaced across the Himalayan region. 

"We will be there for Nepal in its hour of need," he said.  "A comprehensive package of support has been put forward, but we'll continue to work closely with our colleagues in the Nepalese government over the coming hours and days."

33 British nationals are among the missing, according to the Nepalese tourism board. 

Burnham said a 24/7 consulate service had been set up in the capital  Kathmandu to support British nationals in Nepal. 

According to Nepal’s Tourism Board, 517 of the missing people in the country were foreigners and 178 of them were from India.

More than 60 of those unaccounted for in Nepal were from the U.S. and the rest were from 30 other countries, ranging from Ukraine and the U.K. to South Africa and Japan, the board said.

Many of the missing may have been on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus, Buddhists and others.

recentItems.title: Extreme summer heat boosts salt production in Croatia
recentItems.description:
(27 Aug 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS
Nin, Croatia - 21 August 2026

1. Piles of salt, the old city of Nin in background
2. Various of a truck pushing the salt into the pile
3. Various of a salt worker collecting salt and pushing it into a pile
4. SOUNDBITE (Croatian) Mario Salic, salt worker:
“The sun and heat suit us best. The hotter it is, the faster the sea evaporates and the faster the salt is produced.”

5. Various of a worker pushing salt into a pile
6. SOUNDBITE (Croatian) Mario Salic, salt worker:
“Yes, it’s hot, but there’s salt. I think this year will be the best.”

7. Various aerials of the salt fields ++MUTE++
8. Set up shot of Sanja Stamenic Ostric, marketing director, Nin Saltworks
9. SOUNDBITE (Croatian) Sanja Stamenic Ostric, Marketing Director, Nin Saltworks:
“This year is excellent in terms of the harvest. We will have our maximum production of up to 5,000 tons because it was a sunny year and a sunny summer. To produce salt crystals by evaporating seawater, it takes at least 21 sunny days. If there is rain in the meantime, the process takes longer.”

10. Excavator tipping salt onto production line
11. Salt falling from the production belt into a vat
12. Pull focus from conveyor belt to workers in the background 
13. Salt being bagged
14. Close of bag of salt moving on conveyor belt
15. Wide of salt worker lifting bag from conveyor belt
16. Wide of salt worker packing bags of salt
17. SOUNDBITE (Croatian) Sanja Stamenic Ostric, Marketing Director, Nin Saltworks:
“These are old tools that are slowly being forgotten. Usually everything stays in factories, and this is an open-air factory. It’s nice when you can connect with what is produced, when you can feel it, touch it and smell it in the open air.”

18. Sign reading “Nin Saltworks Park”
19. Wide of visitors resting in a gazebo in Nin Saltworks Park
20. Visitors walking past piles of salt
21. Visitor touching salt
22. Visitors walking between salt pools
23. Wide of entrance to the Salt Museum
24. Set up shot of Angela Tartaro, retail manager
25. SOUNDBITE (Croatian) Angela Tartaro, retail manager:
“People are not really aware of the importance of salt and its importance for our health. They are often surprised to learn that our bodies cannot function without salt. I mean, they know it, but when we bring it closer to them, it’s like a light bulb goes off in their heads: ‘Oh yes, that’s right, there’s salt in everything.’ Salt has been around throughout history and will be around long after we are gone.”

26. Wide of visitors walking in Nin Saltworks Park
27. Truck pushing salt onto a pile
28. Wide of salt storage 
29. Visitors walking by the salt storage shed 
30. Close of salt
STORYLINE:
LEADIN 

Searing temperatures have boosted salt production in Croatia this year, with temperatures topping 40 degrees Celsius. 

One company on the Adriatic coast says it has hit maximum production.

STORYLINE 

It looks like snow. White fluffy mounds are moved around by a bulldozer. 

While in much of Croatia, this summer's heatwave has been a problem, there has also been an upside.  

In Nin, on the Adriatic coast, it has delivered a strong salt harvest. 

Salt production relies on seawater, sun and wind. The seawater is channelled into shallow pools, where it slowly evaporates, leaving behind salt crystals.

“The sun and heat suit us best. The hotter it is, the faster the sea evaporates and the faster the salt is produced,” says Mario Salic, a salt worker.

For Salic and his colleagues, this year's weather has been ideal for salt production.

recentItems.title: For everything from troubled hearts to lost keys, Greeks bake cakes for a wish-granting saint
recentItems.description:
(27 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Ilion, Greece - 26 August 2026
1. Aerial of faithful gathering outside church of St. Fanourios ++MUTE++
2. Faithful arriving carrying cakes
3. Priest scoring crosses on cakes 
4. Wide of priest reading prayers as faithful wait with cakes
5. Wide of church bell tower UPSOUND bells ringing
6. Wide of faithful waiting for cakes
7. Pan of cakes on table
8. Wide of faithful taking cakes after blessing
9. Close of cake being cut
10. Mid of woman cutting and giving out cake
11. SOUNDBITE (Greek) Anna Maglara, worshipper: 
“I think St. Fanourios is hope; hope for every person who wants something to be revealed, whatever that may be. Faith is hope, and St. Fanourios - you can see how many people there are. People need to believe in something, to accept help. That is St. Fanourios.”
12. Aerial of faithful gathering with cakes outside church ++MUTE++
13. Close of mosaic of St. Fanourios over church entrance
14. Close of flour being poured into sieve, icon of saint and candle in background
15. Maria Chanioti sifting flour and mixing ingredients in bowl
16. Close of Chanioti orange being juiced
17. Various of Chanioti adding ingredients to bowl
18. Close of Chanioti
19. Wide of Chanioti mixing ingredients
20. Close of spices
21. SOUNDBITE (Greek) Maria Chanioti, worshipper: 
“It is giving thanks to the saint for everything he has given me up to this day, whether good or bad. But more than that, he reveals things to you, and so it is not just that. It is his presence in your life.”
22. Various of Chanioti pouring batter into glass dish
23. Chanioti putting dish into over and making sign of the cross
24. Close of St. Fanourios icon
25. Chanioti taking cake out of oven
26. Chanioti entering church with cake
27. Chanioti approaching Father Nikolaos Vlavianos for cake blessing
28. Close of Chanioti making sign of cross
29. Wide of Chanioti and Nikolaos during blessing
30. Close of St. Fanourios icon
31. Chanioti and Nikolaos
32. Nikolaos scoring cross onto cake

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Ilion, Greece - 25 August 2026
33. Close of St. Fanourios icon and offerings
34. Wide of church
35. Close of cross and candle detail on icon of St. Fanourios
36. SOUNDBITE (Greek) Father Nikolaos Vlavianos, priest:
“Perhaps it is because of the name, as Saint Fanourios, who reveals many things - and not only things - to  people. There are many things that people ask for. We could mention health issues, lost objects, missing people, personal relationships, professional situations. Everyone has something to request of the saint.”
37. Tilt down of icon of St. Fanourios which is a replica of the icon discovered in Rhodes more than 500 years ago, which depicts the saint's suffering as a Christian martyr
38. SOUNDBITE (Greek) Father Nikolaos Vlavianos, priest:
“Many times, it is in the simple, everyday things that the grace of God becomes apparent, which we may consider to be a coincidence and not pay much attention to it. But that is where we see the blessings, we experience them. And if we don’t interpret them as luck, as 'ok, I would have found it,'  we see that the saints even with these seemingly small things, they assist us.”

Ilion, Greece - 26 August 2026

40. Close of cakes
41. Wide of priest and faithful before pan to priest scoring cross on cakes
42. SOUNDBITE (Greek) Vaggelis Fragkoulis, worshippers:
"Love for St. Fanourios, because he gave us health.”
Vaggelis Fragkoulis (Greek): “I had cancer and didn’t know it, and I became well here.”

recentItems.title: Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock pay tribute to Dolly Parton
recentItems.description:
(27 Aug 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS
London - 26 August 2026
1. Wide of Nicole Kidman
2. SOUNDBITE (English) Nicole Kidman, executive producer/actor - on why Parton was special:
"She was so genuine and she was so philanthropic. Great artist. I mean, what a songwriter, what a woman and what a person who came from nothing and built herself. Everything she did was extraordinary. And she will be so missed by all of us. But also the beauty of great, great art, which is what she contributed, is that she will be with us forever. You know, you can listen to her songs and she's right there with you."
3. SOUNDBITE (English) Sandra Bullock, executive producer/actor:
"I've never met anyone that embodied joy. She was honorable. She was honest. She was kind. She's a whole litany of things. But - sorry, - but she lived a life of joy and gratitude. And I said it earlier, I said, 'I don't think people realize what we had. And now that she's no longer with us in body, hopefully we will start living by her example because there's no one else like her. Nobody. Nobody.'"
4. SOUNDBITE (English) Dianne Wiest and Stockard Channing, actors:
Channing: "It's a great loss. Personal for me, and especially Tim Curry, who was a dear friend. But they both led extraordinary lives and in different ways gave back so much to humanity. I think Dolly Parton was an incredible human being."
Wiest: "They'll be missed."
